cases.title: How far away is hydrogen? Its role in the medium and long-term decarbonisation of the European energy system
cases.source_trace: Saved historical abstract; publisher record also verified. Online 2015, journal issue January 2016.
cases.source_specific_proposition: JRC-EU-TIMES scenario modelling suggested hydrogen could become viable in the EU energy system around 2030 under a long-term carbon constraint; hydrogen might help decarbonise industry and transport.
cases.scenario_condition: Long-term carbon cap; scenario is conditional, not a guarantee or the later EU production target.
cases.radar2_question: Has hydrogen become more practically viable as a European decarbonisation option, and what deployment and cost constraints remain on the path to 2030?

findings.document: European Court of Auditors, Special report 11/2024
findings.evidence: The EU was unlikely to meet the 2030 renewable-hydrogen targets established years after the original paper; market rules, project maturity and demand hinder deployment.

findings.document: ACER, European hydrogen markets monitoring report 2025 (covering 2024 deployments)
findings.evidence: EU electrolyser capacity was 308 MW in 2024, 51% more than before but well behind the 2024 EU policy ambition of 6 GW. Renewable hydrogen production costs were about four times conventional hydrogen costs.

findings.document: JRC, Water Electrolysis and Hydrogen in the EU: 2025 Status Report (published 14 Jan 2026)
findings.evidence: EU operational electrolysis capacity was projected at 514–800 MW by end-2025; high capital costs and raw material dependencies remain.

cases.assessment: Hydrogen remains a serious European decarbonisation pathway, but observed rollout and economics lag policy ambition. This is an interim check of the original conditional scenario, not a finding that its 2030 proposition has failed.
cases.scope_caveat: Do not conflate the 2015 model finding with targets set by the EU in 2020–2022; the 2030 horizon is still in the future.

interpretation.similarities: The scenario identified hydrogen as a possible European decarbonisation route and later policy and investment continue to treat it as a serious option.
interpretation.differences: Observed deployment and costs remain much less favourable than EU ambitions, showing practical constraints that the model scenario alone did not establish would be overcome.
interpretation.still_unestablished: The conditional claim about viability in 2030 cannot yet be assessed as fulfilled or failed, and the model carbon-cap condition is not equivalent to later EU hydrogen targets.
interpretation.present_relevance: The original scenario remains a useful conditional pathway, especially for examining carbon constraints, infrastructure bottlenecks and the difference between technical possibility and rollout.

cases.title: Actual and potential development of consumer demand on the organic food market in Europe
cases.source_trace: Saved original abstract, cross-checked against original publisher text. Research covered Denmark, Italy and UK and considered futures up to 2015.
cases.source_specific_proposition: A plausible scenario was continued, relatively stable expansion of organic-food demand, conditional on prices, distribution, consumer trust and public support.
cases.scenario_condition: Qualitative, conditional scenario rather than a fixed volume target.
cases.radar2_question: Did European organic-food consumer demand expand after 2011, how steadily, and do later developments support the factors originally identified?

findings.evidence: Organic retail sales in Europe reached about €26.2 billion in 2014, and the three investigated markets were among the more developed markets.

findings.document: FiBL, The World of Organic Agriculture 2024 (reporting 2022)
findings.evidence: Europe-wide organic retail sales declined by about 2.2% in 2022 rather than rising every year.

findings.document: FiBL, Europe organic market 2024 data released 10 Feb 2026
findings.evidence: European organic retail sales reached €58.7 billion in 2024, above the 2014 value in nominal euros.

cases.assessment: The broad directional expansion appears to have occurred, but stable expansion did not mean uninterrupted annual growth. More directly comparable long-term panels for Denmark, Italy and the UK would be needed to test the consumer barriers identified in the original study.
cases.scope_caveat: Nominal European sales are not inflation-adjusted; wider Europe totals do not prove the specific household-level explanations for Denmark, Italy and the UK.

interpretation.similarities: Later nominal European retail-sales figures support the anticipated broad expansion in demand for organic food.
interpretation.differences: The observed 2022 contraction does not fit an interpretation of stable expansion as uninterrupted annual growth.
interpretation.still_unestablished: Aggregate European nominal sales cannot establish the causal role of the original household-level consumer barriers in Denmark, Italy and the UK.
interpretation.present_relevance: The original questions about prices, distribution and support remain useful, while real-term comparable country panels would be needed to evaluate those explanations.

cases.title: 2022 Strategic Foresight Report: Twinning the green and digital transitions in the new geopolitical context
cases.source_trace: Original institutional source verified online for this pilot. Its excerpt was not stored in the uploaded Radar 2 audit; this review DOES NOT update the live source manifest.
cases.source_specific_proposition: Strategic management and diversification of supplies of critical raw materials would be essential to the EU green and digital transitions; otherwise the EU could fall into new dependency traps.
cases.scenario_condition: A strategic warning and possible future vulnerability, not a numeric prediction.
cases.radar2_question: Did the EU recognise and act on critical raw-material dependencies after 2022, and has actual supply resilience improved?

findings.document: European Critical Raw Materials Act (in force 2024)
findings.evidence: The EU enacted diversification and domestic-capacity policy with non-binding 2030 benchmarks for extraction, processing, recycling and single-country concentration.

findings.document: European Commission strategic-project selections under CRMA
findings.evidence: The Commission designated its first EU strategic-project list on 25 March 2025.

findings.document: European Court of Auditors, Special report 04/2026
findings.evidence: Auditors found diversification had not yet produced tangible results, with obstacles to production and recycling and many projects unlikely to improve supply in time for 2030.

findings.document: European Commission second project selection, 9 Oct 2026
findings.evidence: A further EU list of strategic projects was designated on 9 October 2026; designated projects are not the same thing as delivered supply capacity.

cases.assessment: The risk identified in 2022 generated substantial policy action, while a 2026 independent audit shows the dependency problem remains unresolved. The warning retains strong relevance; the law and announced projects must not be presented as proof of achieved resilience.
cases.scope_caveat: Original foresight was broad; this pilot assesses only one anchored question about critical raw materials, not the whole 2022 report.
cases.original_excerpt: Strategically managing supply of critical materials and commodities, by adopting a long-term systemic approach to avoid a new dependency trap.

passage_review.note: Exact wording of area for action 3 on the original 2022 Commission strategic foresight report webpage.

interpretation.similarities: After the 2022 warning, the EU enacted critical raw-materials legislation and selected projects addressing dependency risks.
interpretation.differences: Subsequent independent evaluation finds tangible diversification and actual resilience still lag the ambition of these policy responses.
interpretation.still_unestablished: Strategic-project designation is not delivered supply capacity; the long-run effect of policy on dependencies is not yet demonstrated.
interpretation.present_relevance: The original warning about a possible dependency trap remains pertinent, and policy implementation should be tracked against actual supply diversification.

cases.title: Suitability of European climate for the Asian tiger mosquito Aedes albopictus: recent trends and future scenarios
cases.source_trace: Original 2012 Royal Society paper abstract checked against PubMed PMID 22535696; source passage preserved in the accepted Radar 1 manifest.
cases.source_specific_proposition: The 2012 climate-suitability scenarios suggested growing risk of Aedes albopictus establishment in northern and north-western Europe, while parts of southern Europe might become less climatically suitable under hotter, drier conditions.
cases.scenario_condition: Conditional projections of climatic suitability, not a forecast of the exact number of established mosquito populations or direct proof of climate-driven spread.
cases.radar2_question: Did Aedes albopictus become established farther north and west in Europe after 2012, and can changes in its distribution be linked specifically to the projected climatic mechanisms?

findings.document: ECDC/EFSA: Aedes albopictus known distribution, June 2025 (published 1 July 2025)
findings.evidence: ECDC reported established Asian tiger mosquito populations in 369 EU/EEA administrative regions across 16 countries, including Belgium, Germany and Austria; it noted newly established populations in Cyprus and Slovakia since the July 2024 update.

findings.document: ECDC/EFSA: Aedes albopictus current known distribution, April 2026 (published 3 June 2026)
findings.evidence: The updated ECDC surveillance map listed established populations in 384 EU/EEA administrative units in 16 countries, fourteen additional units compared with June 2025; the geographic spread remains documented in northern and western EU countries as well as in southern Europe.

findings.document: Farooq et al., The Lancet Planetary Health: Impact of climate and Aedes albopictus establishment on dengue and chikungunya outbreaks in Europe (May 2025)
findings.evidence: A peer-reviewed EU regional analysis of 1990–2024 entomological and outbreak data found shorter intervals between mosquito establishment and first local arbovirus outbreak. Warm-summer conditions were associated with increased outbreak hazard, but this is not proof that temperature alone caused the species to spread north.

cases.assessment: Surveillance reports document substantial expansion and establishment of the Asian tiger mosquito in European regions, including north-western and central European countries, broadly consistent with the direction of the 2012 risk scenarios. But surveillance is not a direct measurement of climatic suitability, and it does not isolate warming from introductions, transport, local habitat and surveillance intensity.
cases.scope_caveat: The southern-Europe part of the scenario cannot be tested by northern establishment counts. Persistent establishment in southern countries does not, by itself, refute a projected decline in suitability. Different map dates, surveillance coverage and administrative boundaries also limit direct counts.

interpretation.similarities: The study anticipated increasing risk in northern Europe. Later ECDC distribution maps identify established populations in several northern or north-western European countries, consistent with that broad direction.
interpretation.differences: The forecast examined potential climatic suitability, whereas the newer data record observed establishment. Human-assisted introductions and surveillance activity can contribute to the distribution regardless of climate trends.
interpretation.still_unestablished: It is not established how much of the expansion was caused by the projected climatic mechanisms, nor whether suitability declined in the specific southern areas highlighted in the 2012 scenarios.
interpretation.present_relevance: The original risk mapping remains useful for planning vector surveillance, but up-to-date establishment records and causal research are needed to guide public-health actions.

cases.title: Assessing the impact of the 2011 EU Transport White Paper - a rail freight demand forecast up to 2050 for the EU27
cases.source_trace: Full original article checked on Springer Nature; published online 19 June 2015 (Radar 1 indexed date 18 June 2015). The optimistic scenario is conditional on EU White Paper modal-shift ambitions.
cases.source_specific_proposition: The 2015 TRANS-TOOLS analysis compared a Reference, a White Paper Low and a White Paper High scenario. Under full achievement of ambitious EU freight modal-shift objectives, the High scenario yielded rail-freight demand nearly twice the Reference scenario by 2050.
cases.scenario_condition: The High case assumes policy implementation, infrastructure capacity and a shift of long-distance freight over 300 km from road toward rail and inland waterways. It is not an unconditional prediction of 2024 modal shares.
cases.radar2_question: Does observed EU rail freight development since 2015 indicate movement toward the ambitious road-to-rail modal shift, and which assumptions of the original High scenario remain unmet?

findings.document: European Environment Agency, Sustainability of Europe’s mobility systems 2025: freight transport activity
findings.evidence: EEA reported rail freight activity of about 396 billion tonne-kilometres in 2023, below its approximately 432 billion tonne-kilometre 2018 peak; rail represented 11.5% of all freight tonne-kilometres under the EEA indicator definition.

findings.document: German Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), EU rail freight modal split, updated 17 March 2026
findings.evidence: Drawing on Eurostat inland-transport data, Destatis reported rail accounted for approximately 17% of EU inland freight tonne-kilometres in 2024, while road accounted for roughly 78%, up from about 74% in 2014. The hoped-for modal shift was not visible in this broad indicator.

cases.assessment: Broad European freight statistics through 2024 do not show a sustained shift toward rail. Road strengthened in the inland-freight modal split while rail activity remained below its 2018 peak. This diverges from the trajectory one would expect under a successfully implemented ambitious White Paper High scenario, but does not establish a numerical test of the study’s >300 km target or its 2050 conditional forecasts.
cases.scope_caveat: EEA overall freight shares and Destatis inland-mode shares have different denominators. Neither directly measures the share of road shipments longer than 300 km transferred to rail, nor the study’s EU27 Trans-Tools 2050 output; do not compare their percentages to the 30%/50% targets as if equivalent.

interpretation.similarities: The original study stressed that major investment and rail-service improvements were needed for a large modal shift. Subsequent monitoring still highlights the challenge of changing European freight’s modal split.
interpretation.differences: Observed inland freight remained increasingly road-oriented through 2024, rather than clearly following the ambitious scenario of rapid and substantial rail demand growth.
interpretation.still_unestablished: The 2030 and 2050 long-distance road-freight shift targets have not reached their final horizons. The broad modal-split datasets do not establish whether the exact >300 km objective is on track.
interpretation.present_relevance: The model remains useful as a conditional picture of what infrastructure, productivity and policy effort would have to accomplish; ongoing freight data can test whether those prerequisites are materialising.

cases.title: Ocean energy development in Europe: Current status and future perspectives
cases.source_trace: Original open-access publisher record checked. The 2015 article describes a sectoral ambition of 100 GW wave-and-tidal capacity by 2050; this is an aspiration reported by the authors, not an unconditional model result.
cases.source_specific_proposition: The 2015 assessment envisaged wave and tidal energy as a potentially substantial contributor to Europe’s future low-carbon electricity system and described a sectoral aim of 100 GW by 2050, conditional on overcoming technology, financing, grid and regulatory barriers.
cases.scenario_condition: A long-term ambition contingent on technology readiness, finance and market development. The objective’s definition and geographical scope need checking before numerical target comparisons.
cases.radar2_question: Did wave and tidal energy move toward large-scale commercial deployment in the EU after 2015, and which originally recognised deployment barriers persist?

findings.document: European Commission DG MARE, EU Blue Economy Report 2025: marine renewable energy
findings.evidence: At the end of 2024, the EU had about 2.82 MW of operational emerging ocean-energy capacity excluding traditional tidal-range projects, including 1.63 MW tidal energy and 1.12 MW wave energy. These technologies remained at demonstration or emerging deployment scale.

findings.document: European Commission Joint Research Centre, Ocean Energy in the European Union — 2025 Status Report (10 December 2025)
findings.evidence: The JRC reviewed the tidal and wave sector’s technical development, EU-funded projects, market progress and bottlenecks through the end of 2024. It identified risks and obstacles to the long-term technology targets, rather than documenting commercial deployment on the original hoped-for scale.

findings.document: Ocean Energy Europe, Ocean energy is moving closer to commercialisation (17 April 2025)
findings.evidence: The European industry association reported five wave and tidal ocean-energy developers deploying new devices in 2024 and a publicly supported 165 MW ocean-energy pipeline planned for deployment over the following five years. These European plans are not operational EU electricity-generating capacity and must not be counted as deployment achieved.

cases.assessment: Wave and tidal energy remain potentially valuable technologies, but observed EU operational emerging capacity at end-2024 was only a few megawatts. That is much closer to an early-stage technology sector than the substantial electricity contribution hoped for in the 2015 discussion. The 2050 ambition is still future-facing and cannot be judged as finally missed.
cases.scope_caveat: The 2.82 MW observation excludes established tidal-range plants such as La Rance. The 100 GW number in the original article is a reported sectoral 2050 aspiration, and project pipelines, installed nameplate power and operational capacity are not interchangeable.

interpretation.similarities: The 2015 study identified technology maturity, finance and market formation as decisive barriers; later EU status reports continue to treat scale-up and deployment bottlenecks as central concerns.
interpretation.differences: The scale of operational wave and tidal installations by 2024 remained small in the EU, far from a mature large-scale energy sector contributing substantially to electricity supply.
interpretation.still_unestablished: It is too early to assess the 2050 ambition conclusively. Later EU targets and historical capacity definitions also need reconciliation before using a numerical achievement ratio.
interpretation.present_relevance: The original work remains useful as a record of the industry’s early hopes and acknowledged constraints. It helps distinguish investment narratives from measured commercial deployment.

policy: Original must be accepted by Radar 1
Original proposition must be grounded in original abstract or document
Subsequent evidence must postdate the original and address same substantive question
Policy or project announcements cannot be called realised outcomes
Keep geography, metrics, original conditions and uncertainty separate
Connection not established is publishable only after documented independent research routes; uninvestigated originals stay unassessed.
